transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Time: 15:00 - 15:45 UTC
Duration: 45 mins
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Ember - Head of ML), Liam O'Connor (Ember - Infra), Sonal Patel (Ember - Security), Jon Park (Ember - Data Eng)

Summary: quick scoping POC to decide deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated vs private). Customer wants clarity on success criteria, workload sizing, benchmarks and timeline. Focus on latency targets for inference, throughput for routing, data residency and encryption controls.

[00:00] Alex Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick round robin? i can start, i'm alex chen, AE at Redwood. priya is our systems engineer.
[00:08] Priya Nair: hi all, priya here. i'll lead on the technical bench and runtime questions.
[00:12] Marta Ruiz: hey alex/priya, this is marta, head of ml at ember logistics. liam, sonal, jon are on.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: liam here, infra lead.
[00:21] Sonal Patel: sonal security. thanks.
[00:23] Jon Park: jon, data eng.

[00:30] Alex Chen: goal for today's call is to understand your success criteria for the POC, the workload size, what benchmarks you want us to run, and then surface the tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated and private. also next steps and timeline.

[01:02] Marta: high level — we're building a realtime ETA/dispatch assistant, so latency matters. we have 3 routes: short chat assistant (small prompts, prefer <150ms tail latency), batch reranks for driver assignment (can be async, throughput more important), and embeddings for search/semantics. budget is a hard constraint - we need to compare per-token cost. we also have data residency — some PII rows can't leave our VPC.

[01:40] Priya: okay, that's helpful. can you give ballpark qps for each route?

[01:45] Jon: sure. chat assistant peaks 40 qps, typical 10 qps. rerank batch runs hourly at about 10k queries over a 15-minute window. embeddings we run nightly - about 200k vectors/day but can be throttled.

[02:10] Priya: great. and latency SLO for the chat is 150ms p95? or p99?

[02:14] Marta: we care about p95 under 150ms, p99 under 250ms ideally. for rerank throughput we want steady 8k QPS sustained across the 15-min window or rather 8k total over that window? (laugh) sorry, bad phrasing. it's 10k jobs in 15 mins, so average ~11/s but bursty - peak could be 600qps for a couple mins.

[02:42] Priya: that's the kind of burstiness we need to plan for. ok quick overview: hosted is fastest to get started — API, no infra to manage. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and can hit low tail latencies with capacity planning. Private (VPC/on-prem) is for locked-down data; you manage networking and we provide a private control plane.

[03:10] Sonal: on the data residency: we have two classes — anonymized telemetry (can be shared to hosted) and identifiable PII (driver/employee info) which cannot leave our VPC. so hybrid approach might be needed.

[03:30] Alex: totally, lots of customers go hybrid: host non-sensitive routes on Redwood hosted API for cost agility and run PII-sensitive workloads on Dedicated or Private. we can route by policy.

[03:45] Marta: question on cost - what's the unit economics? for hosted are we just per token? and for dedicated how do burst and reserved capacity billing work?

[03:56] Priya: yes hosted: per-token + per-embedding unit. Dedicated: commit to GPU pool / reserved instances monthly; you get lower per-token compute and predictable throughput. bursts are handled by burst capacity add-on or overflow to hosted if policy allows. we can run numbers on your actual sample traffic.

[04:20] Liam: on overflow: we don't want PII to spill to hosted. so overflow to hosted only for non-PII routes. can policy do that?

[04:28] Priya: yes, routing policies support per-route tags and data-class tags; you can set fallbacks only for certain classes.

[04:34] Sonal: ok good. next: security controls — SAML/SSO, RBAC, audit logs, KMS for keys, HSM if needed?

[04:43] Alex: we support SSO/SAML, SSO with SCIM provisioning, RBAC roles in the console, full audit logs. for encryption we integrate with customer KMS + there's support for HSM-backed keys for private deployments. we'll share SOC2 and ISO docs.

[04:58] Sonal: do you keep logs in hosted? retention?

[05:02] Priya: audit logs and traces kept per tenancy; retention is configurable. for hosted default retention 90 days; enterprise/Private can extend or ship to your SIEM.

[05:13] Marta: good. let's talk benchmarks — we want Redwood to run a benchmark reflecting our 3 routes. what's the typical POC scope?

[05:21] Priya: we usually do a 2-week POC: week 1 - sizing and smoke tests, week 2 - full benchmark run and QA. For your case we can do a 2-hour benchmark window that simulates peak bursts: chat peak burst at 40 qps, rerank burst up to 600 qps for short window, embeddings throughput for nightly jobs. We'll share harness (k6 + our client) and you share sample payloads.

[05:48] Jon: payloads - note many of our prompts are nested JSON with metadata; also rerank inputs include up to 50 candidates. any input size limits?

[05:58] Priya: runtime supports long contexts; we'll test with your average prompt sizes. for rerank the model selection matters — smaller opt models can rerank cheaper; we'll include a model-variant matrix in the benchmark.

[06:12] Marta: model question — are you recommending single model across routes or variant?

[06:17] Priya: typical is variant: a faster cheaper model for embeddings or rerank, a slightly larger low-latency model or quantized variant for chat. Dedicated is helpful if you want consistent p99 low latencies for chat. Hosted is simpler to start. Private is recommended if data cannot leave your VPC or regulations require on-prem.

[06:40] Liam: performance specifics — if we do Dedicated can we get <150ms p95 for chat?

[06:46] Priya: yes with right GPU type + small batch sizing and KV cache we can hit that. we'll propose GPU SKUs based on the benchmark - typically A10G-style or similar for lower-latency single token generation; for high throughput rerank we recommend higher memory instances and batching.

[07:05] Marta: what's the ramp timeline from POC to Dedicated?

[07:09] Alex: POC 2 weeks, if we validate performance and you approve sizing we can provision Dedicated in 2-4 weeks depending on capacity and contract. Private (VPC) is usually 4-8 weeks due to network and security validation, can be longer for on-prem.

[07:26] Sonal: what about compliance evidence — we need pen test reports and your vendor attestation for our internal procurement.

[07:31] Alex: we'll provide SOC2 type II, ISO27001, pen test summary, and a whitepaper on network architecture. We'll also share our data flow diagrams for review.

[07:44] Jon: how do you do prefix caching / KV cache? we rely on prompt templates heavily, caching could reduce cost and latency if you have repeated prefixes.

[07:52] Priya: our runtime supports KV cache and automatic prefix caching; we can configure TTLs per-route. that often reduces effective token compute for chat. we'll include cache hit metrics in the benchmark.

[08:05] Marta: are there any gotchas for quantized models? we care about quality regression.

[08:10] Priya: we validate quality with prompt-based eval sets; Redwood Optimize provides recommendations and can surface regression alerts tied to eval sets. part of POC we'll run a small eval to ensure quality stays acceptable when using quantized variants.

[08:27] Liam: on cost modeling: we need sample spreadsheet - can you produce a cost comparison for hosted vs dedicated vs private for our traffic?

[08:34] Alex: yes -- we'll run unit economics per-token and include amortized infra for Dedicated and one-time infra costs for Private. we'll send a spreadsheet.

[08:45] Marta: decision criteria in our org — speed to value (how fast we can launch), predictable performance (SLOs), cost efficiency, and security/compliance. above those, timeline to vendor procurement.

[08:58] Sonal: from security POV — if any PII touches hosted, we need data processing addendum and contractual guardrails. otherwise Private.

[09:06] Alex: understood. we have DPA templates and we can annotate routes as city-state residency constraints.

[09:14] Jon: practical note: for rerank and embeddings we might be okay on hosted initially if we anonymize. chat likely Dedicated because of latency.

[09:22] Priya: that hybrid carved route is common. we can show a routing policy example in the follow-up.

[09:28] Marta: if we decide Dedicated, do you help with deployment and testing or is it handoff?

[09:33] Alex: Redwood's Solutions/SE team helps with onboarding. we can do a joint runbook, integration support and 1-2 week shadowing. Dedicated customers get priority on capacity planning and a named CSM.

[09:46] Marta: ok next, timeline: we want POC started next week if possible and a decision meeting with procurement + security 2 weeks after benchmark. Is that feasible?

[09:56] Priya: yes, if you can share sample payloads and SLOs by Friday we can start smoke tests Monday. benchmark the following week.

[10:05] Liam: can you confirm what you need from us?

[10:08] Alex: list: sample payloads for the 3 routes, expected QPS and burst profile, redacted PII examples and which routes are sensitive, SLOs, and contact for procurement. we'll also need an email to share the benchmark harness link.

[10:22] Sonal: i'll share the KMS and compliance checklist.

[10:26] Marta: ok. anything about billing terms for Dedicated in POC? we want to understand if there's a trial credit or discounted commit.

[10:33] Alex: we typically offer trial credits for hosted and a short-term Reserved pilot for Dedicated with a small minimum commitment. exact terms we will include in the pricing doc.

[10:41] Jon: small nit: when you say 'burst capacity add-on', is that pre-provisioned spare capacity or on-demand at higher rates?

[10:47] Priya: it's a burst pool that you can configure; pre-provisioned for guaranteed headroom, or overflow to hosted at on-demand rates depending on policy.

[10:55] Marta: ok sounds reasonable. can you include expected p95/p99 numbers per model SKU in the benchmark report?

[10:59] Priya: yes we'll include model matrix with observed p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens plus recommended quantization profiles.

[11:10] Sonal: do you support bring-your-own-key for hosted? we need BYOK for some credentials if we use hosted.

[11:17] Alex: hosted supports customer-managed KMS for data-at-rest keys on enterprise tier; Private of course lets you own the entire key lifecycle.

[11:24] Marta: ok final recap / next steps?

[11:28] Alex: recap: customer to provide sample payloads, SLOs, and compliance contacts by 2026-03-05. Redwood to send pricing + Dedicated sizing doc by 2026-03-06, provide benchmark harness and run the 2-hour peak simulation week of 2026-03-09. Redwood to share SOC2/ISO and network diagrams.

[11:48] Marta: sounds good. we'll sync procurement after benchmark. thanks.

[11:52] Alex: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with links and action items.

[12:00] -- call ended --

Notes/Artifacts shared: deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/poc-scoping.pdf (shared), benchmark-harness: https://redwood.ai/bench/harness (private link), pricing-spreadsheet: TBD
